name: Storybook
traits: whimsical ink linework with slightly exaggerated proportions
simplified rounded shapes and big readable silhouettes
expressive backgrounds that carry the mood of the page
bestFor: a narrator reading a tale aloud
suits: family, food, toy, book, bedding and gift products; warm, playful, trustworthy brands
stylePara: Hand-illustrated picture-book art: characters with big heads, small hands and rounded simplified bodies drawn in a warm, wobbly ink line; colour laid in opaque gouache with dry-brush edges and coloured-pencil hatching on top for texture; backgrounds painted more loosely than the figures, their colour and shapes bending to the mood, with gently curved walls and leaning furniture; a soft vignette darkens the corners like a printed page; matte surfaces, no gloss; light is warm and painted in, with hand-drawn rim light on the characters.

rendering.line: warm dark-brown ink line of varied weight, a little wobbly, heavier at the bottom of shapes; interior details drawn in fine pencil
rendering.shading: two painted tones per colour plus pencil hatching in the shadows; no smooth rendering
rendering.colour: a harmonious picture-book palette of warm ochres, soft reds and sage greens, with one saturated accent colour per scene; product colours exact
rendering.texture: gouache dry-brush, coloured-pencil grain, visible paper tooth, slight print vignette
rendering.lighting: warm painted light with a hand-drawn rim; the background colour shifts to show mood (golden for comfort, blue for worry)

motion: Animated on twos with a gentle squash and stretch and clear poses held for a beat; secondary motion in hair and leaves is soft and slow; the ink line boils very slightly between drawings; background plates stay still or move as flat layers like a pop-up page.
camera: Framed like a book spread: wide establishing shots, slow lateral pans across a painted plate, gentle push-ins on reactions; parallax in two or three flat layers; no handheld or fast whip moves.
avoid: realistic human proportions and skin pores
printed words on book covers, signs or packaging
eyes and face shapes that change between shots
sheets: A character sheet in the same ink and gouache: front, three-quarter and side plus two expressions, with the head-to-body ratio marked so it does not drift; the place sheet is one painted wide and one detail view; the product is painted in its exact colours with the label kept as plain shapes.
risk: Seedance tends to turn storybook characters into soft 3D family-film figures within a few seconds and to fill bookshelves and signs with fake lettering; repeat 'flat painted gouache, ink line, no 3D' in STYLE and MOTION, keep text off walls, and send a character sheet in every shot because the big-head proportion drifts.

example.prompt: Picture-book illustration still: a rounded, big-headed woman in her thirties with a dark bun and an orange top, drawn in a warm wobbly brown ink line, holds up a small green glass bottle with a yellow cap; a sunny kitchen painted in opaque gouache with gently leaning cupboards and golden window light, a droopy fern on the windowsill with coloured-pencil hatching in its shadows; soft page vignette, matte colours. Vertical 9:16. No text.
